task.name: Automation - {{date}}
task.instructions:
Watson's Order Activity Report — Journal Change Report, PDF, and Email OBJECTIVE Review journal WTJRN in library AITSK00020 for all order header (WTORDH) and order line (WTORDD) changes since 12:00 PM the previous calendar day, produce a Watson's-branded PDF before/after report, and email it to gjones@profoundlogic.com. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 0 — CONNECTION & KNOWN ENVIRONMENT FACTS (read this first, skip discovery) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ \- SQL connection name: "dev" (use via \`aitool sql --input '{connection:"dev", sql:"..."}'\`) \- SSH connection name: "dev" (use via \`ssh dev "system \\"CL COMMAND\\""\` for CL commands) \- Library: AITSK00020 (NOT "AITSK0020" — that name does not exist) \- Journal: WTJRN, library AITSK00020 \- Tables: WTORDH (order header), WTORDD (order line), WTCUST (customer,   for name lookups), WTITEM (item, for description lookups) \- None of these tables have SQL DDL/source in the ibmi-agentic repo — this is   a seeded demo dataset living only in AITSK00020. Don't search the repo for it. \- GOTCHA: AITSK00020 does NOT appear in QSYS2.SYSSCHEMAS or QSYS2.SYSCOLUMNS   on this connection, even though it's fully readable. Don't waste time   "discovering" it via those catalogs or concluding it doesn't exist — just   query AITSK00020.WTORDH / AITSK00020.WTORDD directly with SELECT \*, it works   fine. If you ever need to re-verify field layout, use   \`SELECT OBJNAME FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT\_STATISTICS('QSYS','\*LIB','AITSK00020'))\`   or \`DSPFFD\` over SSH (see field layouts below — you shouldn't need to rerun   DSPFFD unless the decode below looks wrong, which would mean the table   structure changed). \- aitool sql quoting gotcha: SQL string literals must use single quotes   (double quotes are identifier delimiters in Db2 for i SQL). Wrap the whole   --input value in double quotes and escape inner double quotes, e.g.:   aitool sql --input "{connection:\\"dev\\", sql:\\"SELECT \* FROM AITSK00020.WTORDH WHERE ORDER\_NUMBER = 5001\\"}" ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 1 — COMPUTE THE TIME WINDOW ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Window = \[yesterday 12:00:00 PM, now\].   aitool sql --input "{connection:\\"dev\\", sql:\\"VALUES CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP\\"}"   aitool sql --input "{connection:\\"dev\\", sql:\\"VALUES CURRENT\_DATE - 1 DAY\\"}" Build STARTING\_TIMESTAMP as '-12.00.00.000000' in the 'YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.NNNNNN' format DISPLAY\_JOURNAL expects. Record the current timestamp too — it goes in the report header and email subject. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 2 — PULL JOURNAL ENTRIES (WTORDH + WTORDD only, UB/UP pairs) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ GOTCHA: JRNCDE(J) + ENTTYP(UB UP) fails with CPF7065. Before/after record images are JRNCDE(R). Also: QSYS2.DISPLAY\_JOURNAL's ENTRY\_DATA is a raw BLOB with zero automatic decoding — you must decode it yourself (Step 3). First get a cheap inventory of what changed (no BLOB yet, fast):   aitool sql --input "{connection:\\"dev\\", sql:\\"SELECT OBJECT, JOURNAL\_ENTRY\_TYPE, ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP FROM TABLE(QSYS2.DISPLAY\_JOURNAL('AITSK00020','WTJRN', STARTING\_TIMESTAMP=>'')) WHERE JOURNAL\_ENTRY\_TYPE IN ('UB','UP') AND OBJECT LIKE 'WTORD%' ORDER BY ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP\\"}" If zero rows: skip to Step 6 and send a short "no order header/line changes in this window" email instead of a full report — still send something, so the recipient has confirmation the job ran. Otherwise continue. Then pull full ENTRY\_DATA for those same entries (needed for decode):   aitool sql --input "{connection:\\"dev\\", sql:\\"SELECT ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP, JOURNAL\_ENTRY\_TYPE, OBJECT, ENTRY\_DATA FROM TABLE(QSYS2.DISPLAY\_JOURNAL('AITSK00020','WTJRN', STARTING\_TIMESTAMP=>'')) WHERE JOURNAL\_ENTRY\_TYPE IN ('UB','UP') AND OBJECT LIKE 'WTORD%' ORDER BY ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP\\"}" > /tmp/wtord\_entries.json ENTRY\_DATA comes back as {"type":"Buffer","data":\[...byte values...\]} — a plain byte array, decode it in Python (Step 3). Ignore WTITEM/WTCUST journal noise in the same window (WTITEM in particular gets frequent unrelated bulk price/qty refreshes) — this report is scoped to WTORDH/WTORDD only. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 3 — DECODE THE RAW JOURNAL IMAGES (exact field layouts, already known) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Confirmed via DSPFFD on 2026-07-23. If decoded values look garbled/wrong, the physical file changed shape — rerun \`ssh dev "system \\"DSPFFD FILE(AITSK00020/WTORDH)\\""\` (and WTORDD) to refresh these offsets before trusting any output. WTORDH (record length 430), field: type, buffer length, buffer position(1-based), nullable:   ORDNO bin 4 1 no   CUSTNO bin 4 5 no   ORDDT date 10 9 no (ISO text in buffer, \*ISO date format)   REQSDT date 10 19 yes   ACTSDT date 10 29 yes   ORDSTA varchar 12 39 no (alloc 10)   PONBR varchar 22 51 no (alloc 20)   OADDR1 varchar 42 73 no (alloc 40)   OADDR2 varchar 42 115 no (alloc 40)   OCITY varchar 32 157 no (alloc 30)   OSTATE char 2 189 no   OZIP varchar 12 191 no (alloc 10)   SADDR1 varchar 42 203 no (alloc 40)   SADDR2 varchar 42 245 no (alloc 40)   SCITY varchar 32 287 no (alloc 30)   SSTATE char 2 319 no   SZIP varchar 12 321 no (alloc 10)   ORDTOT packed\_2dec 6 333 no   CRTAT timestamp 26 339 no   CRTBY varchar 20 365 no (alloc 18)   UPDAT timestamp 26 385 no   UPDBY varchar 20 411 no (alloc 18) WTORDD (record length 156):   ORDNO bin 4 1 no   LINNBR bin 4 5 no   KITPLN bin 4 9 yes   KITSEQ bin 4 13 yes   SKU char 10 17 no   QTYORD packed\_2dec 5 27 no   QTYALC packed\_2dec 5 32 no   QTYSHP packed\_2dec 5 37 no   UNTPRC packed\_2dec 5 42 no   EXTPRC packed\_2dec 6 47 no   LINSTA varchar 12 53 no (alloc 10)   CRTAT timestamp 26 65 no   CRTBY varchar 20 91 no (alloc 18)   UPDAT timestamp 26 111 no   UPDBY varchar 20 137 no (alloc 18) Null-value indicator: DISPLAY\_JOURNAL doesn't expose NULL\_VALUE\_INDICATORS per-field cleanly from the table function in a documented way — in practice ACTSDT decodes to '0001-01-01' when null/unshipped; treat that literal as "not yet shipped" rather than a real date. KITPLN/KITSEQ similarly decode to 0 for non-kit lines; treat 0 as "not a kit component." Decode script (Python, run with plain python3 — no special deps needed for this part):   import json   def ebcdic(b): return bytes(b).decode('cp037')   def bin\_int(b): return int.from\_bytes(bytes(b), 'big', signed=True)   def packed(b):       s = bytes(b).hex()       digits, sign = s\[:-1\], s\[-1\]       val = int(digits) if digits else 0       return -val if sign in ('d', 'b') else val   def get(buf, pos, length): return buf\[pos-1:pos-1+length\]   WTORDH\_FIELDS = \[       ('ORDNO','bin',4,1),('CUSTNO','bin',4,5),('ORDDT','date',10,9),       ('REQSDT','date',10,19),('ACTSDT','date',10,29),       ('ORDSTA','varchar',12,39),('PONBR','varchar',22,51),       ('OADDR1','varchar',42,73),('OADDR2','varchar',42,115),       ('OCITY','varchar',32,157),('OSTATE','char',2,189),       ('OZIP','varchar',12,191),('SADDR1','varchar',42,203),       ('SADDR2','varchar',42,245),('SCITY','varchar',32,287),       ('SSTATE','char',2,319),('SZIP','varchar',12,321),       ('ORDTOT','packed\_2dec',6,333),('CRTAT','timestamp',26,339),       ('CRTBY','varchar',20,365),('UPDAT','timestamp',26,385),       ('UPDBY','varchar',20,411),   \]   WTORDD\_FIELDS = \[       ('ORDNO','bin',4,1),('LINNBR','bin',4,5),('KITPLN','bin',4,9),       ('KITSEQ','bin',4,13),('SKU','char',10,17),       ('QTYORD','packed\_2dec',5,27),('QTYALC','packed\_2dec',5,32),       ('QTYSHP','packed\_2dec',5,37),('UNTPRC','packed\_2dec',5,42),       ('EXTPRC','packed\_2dec',6,47),('LINSTA','varchar',12,53),       ('CRTAT','timestamp',26,65),('CRTBY','varchar',20,91),       ('UPDAT','timestamp',26,111),('UPDBY','varchar',20,137),   \]   def decode\_record(raw, fields):       out = {}       for name, typ, blen, pos in fields:           chunk = get(raw, pos, blen)           if typ == 'bin':               out\[name\] = bin\_int(chunk)           elif typ in ('date', 'timestamp'):               out\[name\] = ebcdic(chunk)           elif typ == 'char':               out\[name\] = ebcdic(chunk).rstrip()           elif typ == 'varchar':               ln = int.from\_bytes(bytes(chunk\[:2\]), 'big')               out\[name\] = ebcdic(chunk\[2:2+ln\])           elif typ.startswith('packed'):               scale = int(typ.split('\_')\[1\]\[0\])               out\[name\] = packed(chunk) / (10 \*\* scale)       return out   rows = json.load(open('/tmp/wtord\_entries.json'))\['data'\]\['rows'\]   decoded = \[\]   for row in rows:       raw = row\['ENTRY\_DATA'\]\['data'\]       fields = WTORDH\_FIELDS if row\['OBJECT'\].strip().startswith('WTORDH') else WTORDD\_FIELDS       decoded.append({           'ts': row\['ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP'\], 'type': row\['JOURNAL\_ENTRY\_TYPE'\],           'object': row\['OBJECT'\].strip()\[:6\], 'rec': decode\_record(raw, fields),       }) Pair up consecutive UB/UP entries with the same ENTRY\_TIMESTAMP (a UB is always immediately followed by its matching UP) to get before/after per change. Group changes by ORDNO across both files so a header total change and its causing line change land in the same section of the report. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 4 — ENRICH WITH CUSTOMER NAMES AND ITEM DESCRIPTIONS ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ For every distinct CUSTNO seen, look up the name:   SELECT CUSTOMER\_NUMBER, CUSTOMER\_NAME FROM AITSK00020.WTCUST WHERE CUSTOMER\_NUMBER IN (...) For every distinct SKU seen, look up the description/brand:   SELECT SKU, SHORT\_DESCRIPTION, ITEM\_DESCRIPTION, BRAND, UNIT\_PRICE FROM AITSK00020.WTITEM WHERE SKU IN (...) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 5 — BUILD THE PDF (Watson's brand look, via the /pdf skill) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Brand palette (matches watsons.com — navy/orange leisure-retail look):   Navy: #0F2A4A Orange accent: #F4A300 / #B8590A   Light header tint: #D9E2EC Card background: #F2F2F2 Setup (fpdf2 is not preinstalled and this container is PEP-668 externally managed — do NOT \`pip install --break-system-packages\`; use a venv):   python3 -m venv /tmp/pdfenv   /tmp/pdfenv/bin/pip install --quiet fpdf2   /tmp/pdfenv/bin/python3 ~/.claude/skills/pdf/pdf\_generate.py @/tmp/spec.json Known /pdf skill (fpdf2 2.8.7) bugs to design around — do not fight these, just avoid triggering them:   1. \`\` INSIDE a \`\`/\`\` is silently ignored (always      renders black). Put colored, bold text OUTSIDE table cells (plain      \`...\` paragraphs work perfectly). Inside      \`\`, only use \`bgcolor\` + default black text.   2. A \`\` with more than one child tag (e.g. \`A
B\`)      throws \`NotImplementedError\`. Keep at most one simple tag      (\`\` or \`\`, not both nested) with one contiguous text run per \`\`.   3. Core Helvetica font can't render em-dash "—"/"—", bullet "•", or      arrow "→"/"→" — throws FPDFUnicodeEncodingException. Use ASCII:      "-" for dashes, "\*" for bullets, "->" for arrows.   4. Use the JSON "html" content type with a real \`\` (not the native      "table" content type) for any cell with more than a couple words — the      native "table" type doesn't wrap text and cells will visually collide.   5. Section-header "card" pattern that works well (navy accent bar + light      card, bold black text, no color-in-td bug):      
                         
 Order #NNNN - Name (Customer #NNNN)
Report structure:   1. Masthead: plain (non-table) colored heading "WATSON'S" (navy, bold,      size ~28) + "POOL \* PATIO \* SPA" (orange, bold, size ~11), then a thin      full-width orange accent bar (\` \`).   2. Title "Order Activity Report" + subtitle with the actual date range      covered (yesterday 12:00 PM through now).   3. A metadata table: window covered / journal source (WTJRN in AITSK00020)      / count of orders affected.   4. Executive summary paragraph (plain text, 2-4 sentences) naming each      order changed and the net effect.   5. One section per affected order: navy/card header with order #, customer      name, customer #; a status/total/updated-timestamp line in grey; an      orange bold "Change: ..." one-line description; a Field/Before/After      HTML table (wraps automatically); a short italic explanation paragraph.   6. Closing orange banner "What Changed, In Short" + bulleted recap.   7. Footer line citing the exact journal/entry-type/window used for      traceability. Render to PNG with \`pdftoppm -png -r 120 out.pdf preview\` and visually review every page before emailing — check for text overflow/clipping and correct colors, per the bugs above. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 6 — EMAIL ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Via the /email skill, to gjones@profoundlogic.com. Subject: "Watson's Order Activity Report - to ( Orders Changed)" Body: HTML, one bullet per order summarizing the change (mirrors the PDF's "What Changed, In Short" section), plus a line noting the PDF is attached with full before/after detail. Attachment: the generated PDF. If zero changes were found in Step 2, send a short email instead noting no order header/line changes occurred in the window (no PDF needed). ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ STEP 7 — CLEANUP ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Do not create any objects in AITSK00020 or AIDEMOBASE. If you use any scratch outfile for troubleshooting, create it only in this session's own IBMI\_BUILD\_LIBRARY task library and delete it (\`DLTF\`) before finishing. No source files in the ibmi-agentic repo should be touched by this task — if you find yourself about to edit repo source, stop, this task doesn't need it. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Follow the standard /task-output/summary.md requirements (IBM i task library name, no exploratory-verification section needed since no interactive screens are involved, no commit-message.txt since no repo changes are expected).
